finding.title: Out-of-order archive revisions make unchanged rescrape admission depend on input order
finding.mechanism: append_observations initializes latest_signature by overwriting each revision_key in archive line order, not by observation availability/revision clock. _semantic_signature intentionally excludes available_at_ms, observed_at_ms and revision. A batch [newer,older] leaves the older value as latest_signature; a later unchanged rescrape of newer semantics is admitted, whereas [older,newer] suppresses it. Existing replay test covers chronological base->unchanged->changed, not reversed batch order.
finding.fixture: Use tempfile observations.jsonl; FlowObservation family=etf, metric=net_flow_usd, asset=BTC, unit=USD, source=fixture, source_record_id=day1, effective_at_ms=86400000, provenance={collector:fixture}. older: value=10, revision=r1, available_at_ms=864000000, observed_at_ms=864000000. newer: value=12, revision=r2, available_at_ms=1036800000, observed_at_ms=1036800000. rescrape: value=12, revision=r2, available_at_ms=1123200000, observed_at_ms=1123200000. Seed each order in separate fresh archives; append rescrape after seeding.
expected_assertions: Both initial orderings admit exactly two distinct semantic revisions and preserve original available/observed timestamps and provenance.
Appending rescrape after either order returns zero, with exactly two archived rows; no synthetic same-value revision merely from a later scrape clock.

Existing source implementation is expected to violate the preceding assertion only for [newer,older]: it returns one and grows archive to three; record as expected regression failure, not an executed test.
Strict JSONL reload succeeds; replay at time between older and newer availability sees older value, after newer availability sees newer value, independent of input order.
Subsequent no-network run_once/retry publishes latest.json, audit_latest.json and anata_latest.json coherently without order-dependent archive inflation; exact duplicates append zero.
